deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1983–84 notes, Grothendieck studies finite 'systems of pseudo-lines' Σ = (X, Σ): a family of n pseudolines D in a (topological) projective plane X, with Σ written as D_Σ. On the previous page he builds a 'déploiement' (unfolding) of Σ in three steps:
- He multiplies each D into as many copies as it has vertices, one for each contact element (D, s).
- He glues in local cells: a topological bigon at each simple crossing, and a convex topological 2k-gon at each multiple point.
- The result is a compact surface 𝒳(Σ).

What this page does. It tries to axiomatize the output of that construction. The surface 𝒳 carries two sub-complexes K and L, each giving a cellular decomposition of 𝒳. The listed properties are:
- (a) K is 4-valent. Its 'déploiement' K' is described as a zigzag contour.
- (a') All vertices of L have even order, with no finite loops. L plays the role of the (blown-up) pseudoline arrangement, and the order 2k of a vertex encodes a k-fold crossing.
- (b) Each edge of K contains at most one vertex of L.
- (c) Call an edge of K 'exceptional' if it contains no vertex of L. The closure K_0 of the exceptional edges is a finite disjoint union of circles. Every vertex of K has at least one 'ordinary' outgoing edge.
- (d) The union K_1 of the closures of the ordinary edges is related to K'. A normal-bundle / band-bundle ('fibré des bandes') argument gives a section, i.e. an embedding K'_1 ↪ 𝒳. A pseudoline has a Möbius-band neighbourhood in RP², so the band bundle is the natural tubular structure.
- (e) Behaviour of L near an exceptional vertex s of K: on the contiguous non-exceptional edges, s carries the multiplicities of the neighbouring L-points.
- (f) If x ∈ K∩L, then K has two branches at x, and x is a point of even order of L. This gives three local pictures, drawn in colour (green = K, red = L):
  - (α) x ∉ S(L) (order 2 in L), hence x ∉ S(K);
  - (β) x ∈ S(L) \ S(K);
  - (γ) x ∈ S(L) ∩ S(K).
- (f') Exceptional vertices of K are not in L.
- (g) At an ordinary vertex s of K, the four ordinary edges leaving s see the same 'reduced multiplicity' ν(s) of L. Set ε(s) = 1 if s ∈ L and 0 otherwise.
- (h) Let n be the order (number of pseudolines) of Σ. Then for every face F of K, the number of L-points on ∂F, counted with reduced multiplicity, is 2n. Explicitly:
  Σ_{s singular on F} (2ν(s) + ε(s)) + Σ_{edges a of F} ν(a) = 2n.
  This is the combinatorial shadow of the fact that a closed curve surrounding the arrangement in RP² crosses each of the n pseudolines twice.

Purpose. This is a working attempt to characterize abstractly, by local incidence data of two transverse cell decompositions, the surfaces that arise as unfoldings of pseudoline arrangements. Such a characterization would allow reconstructing Σ from (𝒳, K, L).
errors: The date reads 31.11.83, but November has only 30 days. Either Grothendieck slipped or the transcription misreads it (possibly 21.11 or 30.11).

The page is a draft with many struck-out and reworded conditions (c)/(d). The relation between K_0, K_1 and K' is not stated consistently, and condition (h) is first formulated with ν(a) = ν(s)+ν(s'), then deleted and rewritten. As written, the axioms are not shown to be sufficient for reconstructing Σ; no proof is given.

The count 2n in (h) presupposes that every face of K 'sees' all n pseudolines twice. This is plausible for faces surrounding the whole arrangement, but is asserted, not verified, for all faces (the note 'ND si F ordinaire' suggests a restriction to ordinary faces).

ideas.what: Unfolding ('déploiement') of a pseudoline arrangement into a compact surface by replacing simple crossings with bigons and k-fold points with convex 2k-gons, after multiplying each line by its number of vertices
ideas.modern_name: resolution/truncation of multiple points; closely related to the dual rhombic/zonotopal tiling of a pseudoline arrangement and to wiring diagrams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dual zonotopal tilings: Bohne–Dress (c. 1989–92); wiring diagrams/allowable sequences: Goodman–Pollack (1980s)

ideas.what: Axiomatization of a surface carrying two transverse cellular decompositions K (4-valent) and L (even valence) with local incidence conditions
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial characterization of arrangement surfaces / medial-graph-type structures (4-regular graph with its checkerboard companion)

ideas.what: Face-boundary count: weighted number of L-points on ∂F equals 2n
ideas.modern_name: elementary Euler/degree counting for pseudoline arrangements in RP² (each pseudoline met twice by a large circle)

ideas.what: Use of the band bundle (Möbius-band neighbourhoods) of pseudolines to embed the ordinary part K'_1 into the surface

missed.claim: An abstract characterization of the unfolding surface 𝒳(Σ) of a pseudoline arrangement by the pair of cell decompositions (K, L) and local axioms (a)–(h), intended to make Σ recoverable from (𝒳, K, L). The list is left incomplete and unproved.
missed.quote: Déploiement d'un syst. de pseudo-droites ... surface compacte 𝒳=𝒳(Σ), avec deux sous-complexes K, L tels que K, L décomposent cellulairement 𝒳
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean intrinsic characterization of such 'arrangement surfaces' would give an alternative, surface-topological encoding of rank-3 oriented matroids. This would complement the zonotopal-tiling (Bohne–Dress) and wiring-diagram encodings, but its novelty relative to those is uncertain.

missed.claim: The replacement of each k-fold point by a convex 2k-gon, and simple points by bigons, anticipates the dual zonogonal tiling picture of pseudoline arrangements.
missed.quote: trois cas de figures pour un x∈K∩L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedent (1983) for tiling/dual-surface encodings of pseudoline arrangements, independent of the oriented-matroid school. It is of mainly historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of an axiomatization of a combinatorial construction on pseudoline arrangements. The ideas are natural and close to later standard encodings (dual tilings, wiring diagrams). Nothing here is a finished result that a specialist would find surprising, though it documents Grothendieck's independent topological approach.
transcription_corrections: The date '31.11.83' is likely misread or a slip; check whether it is 21.11.83 or 30.11.83.

Margin note at left reads roughly 'cette donnée équivaut au fait des arêtes ... et positions des pts' (a remark that the data equals the arrangement of edges and positions of points), not as transcribed.
In (f), the order condition on x in L is 'd'ordre pair' (even order) of L, consistent with (a'), rather than '≥4 / impair'.
The three coloured figures on the right are labelled b), a), c) top to bottom and correspond to the cases α) x∉S(L), β) x∈S(L)∖S(K), γ) x∈S(L)∩S(K) listed at the bottom.
